source.summary: A new road bridge across the Tumen river opened to traffic on Monday, connecting Russia and North Korea. Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin stated the crossing was built in record time and can handle up to 300 vehicles daily. North Korean Prime Minister Pak Thae-song noted the project was completed in 495 days. The structure, including access roads, spans 5 km total, with the bridge itself measuring about 1 km. An agreement to build the bridge was signed in 2024, with construction beginning in spring 2025.

source.summary: The Supreme Court refused to pause the implementation of a new UPI merchant discount rate regime effective October 15, declining a plea to stay the decision. The court issued notices to the Centre, RBI, and NPCI, asking them to respond within four weeks regarding the legal and technical basis for the fee on transactions above Rs 2,000. While the petitioner challenged the framework's validity and lack of consultation, the bench observed it was more a technical issue. The government defended the move, stating 96% of users are exempt and no money is taken directly by the state. The court sought a counter-affidavit to understand the executive basis for the charge.

source.summary: Five people died when an Amazon cargo jet ran off the runway at Miami International Airport and struck a shuttle van used by an aircraft cleaning crew. Miami-Dade County Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz confirmed the identities of the deceased, while the National Transportation Safety Board Chairwoman Jennifer Homendy announced that the investigation will center on the lack of specialized deceleration systems. Although the airport maintains a safety buffer, it lacks lightweight crushable materials found at other US airfields. Homendy emphasized that recommendations must be implemented to prevent future tragedies. Investigators have recovered the flight data recorder and are scheduling interviews with the crew and witnesses. Two victims remain in critical condition, while the pilots have been released from the hospital.
source.title: Five Miami plane crash victims identified as Amazon jet ran off runway

source.summary: Databricks prioritized providing its 14,000 employees with instant access to new frontier AI models, a challenge the company described as nontrivial for large organizations. To manage this rollout, the company utilized its internal Unity Gateway platform to adaptively release and evaluate models like Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Sol. During a critical test week in late September, the company granted Day 1 access to these models, tagging them as experimental. Within three days, data collection confirmed the models were on the efficiency frontier, leading to their incorporation into broader infrastructure. The company plans to make Opus 5.5 the default for Claude Code due to its superior quality and lower cost, while integrating GPT-6 Sol into a smart router toolkit.
source.title: Databricks Deploys Frontier AI Models to 14,000 Employees on Day One

source.summary: Bank unions deferred a proposed three-day nationwide strike scheduled for late September 2026 following discussions with bank managements. The United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) announced an understanding with the Indian Banks' Association (IBA), though the strike remains uncancelled as demands are not yet fully met. Key issues include implementing a five-day work week and revising the Performance Linked Incentive scheme. A high-level committee comprising representatives from both the IBA and UFBU has been constituted to examine these demands and work out a mutually acceptable solution.
